title: Hands reached out to harm you, and Allah held them back.
subtitle: Remembering the harm that never arrived
then: Jabir reported that the Prophet ﷺ rested under a tree and hung his sword on it. A bedouin man took the sword, raised it and asked: who can protect you from me? {idea}The Prophet ﷺ answered: Allah.{/idea} The man lowered the sword, and {reward}the Prophet ﷺ did not punish him.{/reward}
now: The car that braked just in time. The scan that came back clear. The plan against you at work that fell apart before you even heard of it. {idea}Most of the harm you were saved from, you never saw.{/idea}
old: Bad things that did not happen are not worth thinking about.
new: Every harm that missed me is a favor to remember, and a reason to rely on Him.
try: Write down one close call from your life and thank Allah for it by name.

title: I am with you, if you keep your side.
subtitle: A covenant with twelve leaders and a clear offer
then: Allah took a pledge from the Children of Israel through twelve leaders, one for each tribe. Ibn Kathir notes that on the night of Aqabah, {idea}twelve leaders of the Ansar{/idea} also gave the pledge to the Prophet ﷺ for their people. The offer was the same: {reward}I am with you{/reward}, if you pray, give and support the truth.
now: You are the one your family calls when things fall apart. Or the one who leads the team meeting. {idea}Leadership starts with keeping your own promise first.{/idea} The verse says His support travels with the one who keeps his side.
old: Allah is with me no matter what I do.
new: He offers to be with me, and my prayer, charity and loyalty are my side of it.
try: Give a small amount in charity today, quietly, as your part of the pledge.

title: Broken promises harden hearts. Pardon anyway.
subtitle: What breaking a covenant does inside a person
then: Right after the offer of verse 12, this verse tells what happened when the pledge was broken: {trap}hearts grew hard, words were twisted, and parts of the reminder were forgotten.{/trap} Yet the Prophet ﷺ is told: {idea}pardon them and overlook.{/idea}
now: You skip the prayer once and it hurts. By the tenth time you feel nothing. {trap}That numbness is the hardening.{/trap} And when someone breaks a promise to you, the verse still asks you to {idea}pardon and do good.{/idea}
old: Breaking small promises does not change who I am.
new: Each broken promise hardens me a little, and pardoning others softens me back.
try: Pardon one person today for a small broken promise. Tell them, or just let it go in your heart.

title: Forget part of the reminder, and people turn on each other.
subtitle: What happens to a community that drops the core
then: Like verse 13, this is about a covenant taken and {trap}part of the reminder forgotten.{/trap} The result was not punishment from outside, but {trap}enmity and hatred among themselves.{/trap} Allah will tell each one what they used to do.
now: The family that stopped eating together. The mosque committee that argues about everything except the reason it exists. {idea}When the shared core is forgotten, small things become wars.{/idea} The question is what part of the reminder you have let slip.
old: Our fights are about the other person being difficult.
new: Division often begins when we forget what we were reminded of together.
try: Bring back one shared good habit with family or friends this week, like a meal or a prayer together.

title: He made much clear, and let much pass.
subtitle: A light and a clear Book, delivered with restraint
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the Prophet ﷺ made clear what had been hidden or changed, and {reward}passed over much of it, since explaining it would bring no benefit.{/reward} With him came {idea}a light and a clear Book{/idea} for all people.
now: Your friend's story has a few errors. Your coworker's report has small mistakes. {trap}You want to correct every one in front of everyone.{/trap} The verse shows another way: {idea}say what matters, and let the rest go.{/idea}
old: Being truthful means pointing out every mistake I see.
new: Truth is clarity on what matters, with mercy on what does not.
try: Next time you notice a small mistake in someone today, let it pass without comment.

title: Seek His pleasure and you are led to paths of peace.
subtitle: From many darknesses into one light
then: This continues verse 15: the light and the clear Book. Ibn Kathir says the paths of peace are {reward}ways of safety and righteousness{/reward}, and that Allah {idea}brings people out of darkness into light{/idea}, rescuing them from ruin and showing them the clearest path.
now: Three in the morning, too many worries at once: money, health, a falling-out. {trap}Darkness comes in layers.{/trap} The verse says the light is one, and {idea}the door to it is wanting what pleases Him.{/idea}
old: I need to solve all my problems before I can feel at peace.
new: Peace begins when I turn toward what pleases Him, and He leads me out.
try: Tonight before sleep, ask Allah for guidance in one worry by name.

title: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him alone.
subtitle: No created being shares the Creator's place
then: The verse answers a claim about Isa, son of Maryam. Ibn Kathir explains it by reminding of {idea}Allah's perfect power over everything.{/idea} Who could stop Him? {reward}All things in existence are His property and creation.{/reward}
now: A favorite scholar, a parent, a doctor, a celebrity. You may never call anyone a god, but {trap}you can still hang your whole heart on a person.{/trap} The verse puts every creature, however loved, {idea}under His dominion.{/idea}
old: The people I admire most could never let me down.
new: Every person I admire is a creation of Allah, and He alone holds everything.
try: Think of one person you depend on too much. Ask Allah directly for what you usually ask them.

title: Being loved is not a pass. You are still accountable.
subtitle: No group label replaces your own deeds
then: Some among the People of the Book said they were Allah's children and beloved. Ibn Kathir explains the reply: {idea}you are human beings like the rest of the children of Adam.{/idea} Allah is Lord of all, and {trap}none can escape His judgment.{/trap}
now: You come from a religious family. Your father is an imam. You go to the right mosque. {trap}It is easy to feel safe by association.{/trap} The verse turns the question back to you: {idea}what are you doing with it?{/idea}
old: Because of where I come from, I am already among the good ones.
new: I am a human being like everyone else, and my deeds return to Allah with me.
try: Do one good deed today that no one would expect from your background or your label.

title: After a long silence, a messenger came. No excuse remains.
subtitle: Good news and warning, delivered when most needed
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Salman Al-Farisi that about {trap}six hundred years passed between Isa and Muhammad ﷺ{/trap} with no messenger. The world was full of confusion. Sending the Prophet ﷺ then was {reward}the perfect favor, when he was needed most.{/reward}
now: You know more about Islam than most people in history ever could. The Quran is in your pocket. {trap}The excuse that no one told me does not fit anymore.{/trap} {idea}The message has arrived, with good news first.{/idea}
old: I did not grow up knowing much, so I cannot be expected to act on it.
new: The message has reached me now, with good news and a warning, and that is a gift.
try: Read one verse today with its meaning, slowly, as if it were just delivered to you.

title: Remember the favors. You are richer than you think.
subtitle: Musa counts his people's blessings before the hard test
then: Before asking his people to move forward, Musa reminded them of {reward}Allah's favors on them.{/reward} Ibn Abbas said made you kings means {idea}having a house, a wife and a servant.{/idea} A hadith says that whoever wakes healthy, safe in his family, with food for the day, has been given the world.
now: You woke up today. Your body works. Your family is safe. There is food in the fridge. {trap}Yet you scroll and feel poor.{/trap} By the measure in this verse, {idea}you are living like a king.{/idea}
old: I will feel blessed once I have more than I have now.
new: A safe home, health and today's food already make me rich.
try: Before your next meal, name three things you have that make you a king by this measure.
